newsitem.title: USA: Phillips posts higher profits fueled by tax gains.
newsitem.headline: Phillips posts higher profits fueled by tax gains.

text.p: Phillips Petroleum Co. on Thursday posted higher second-quarter earnings, fuelled byan $80 million one-time gain from the resolution of a long-running tax dispute.
The Bartlesville, Okla.-based oil company reported $307 million, or $1.17 a share, in second- quarter net income, up from $221 million, or 84 cents a share, in the same period last year.

The second-quarter earnings reflect $93 million in special items, including an $80 million tax resolution for the years 1983 to 1986 tied to income from the company's interest in a Kenai, Alaska, liquefied natural gas facility.

Excluding the one-time items, however, operating income fell to $214 million, from $221 million a year ago, hurt by lower crude oil prices and natural gas production and higher exploration expenses. Total revenues fell to $3.8 billion from $4 billion in the same period last year.

Chairman Wayne Allen said Phillips is nearing a deal with Petroleos de Venezuela SA (PDVSA) on a joint venture to upgrade the U.S. oil company's Sweeney, Texas, refinery. PDVSA is the government-owned oil company of Venezuela.
The deal, valued at $400 million to $500 million, would include the addition of a coker at the 185,000 barrel per day refinery to process heavy Venezuelan crude oil, Allen said.

"It's (a) four or five hundred million dollars, highly financed joint venture," Allen said of the deal. "It's attractive, though, because it gives us some capability to run the heavier crudes and optimize our crude slate."
The upgrade is part of Phillips' push to boost refining margins and position its operations for an ongoing consolidation in the U.S. refining business, he said.

"We don't plan to exit the business, so we approach it like we are going to keep it forever. Obviously, if there was a business opportunity where we could spread our overheads over a larger volume base, we would do it," he said. "That's really what these alliances and mergers are all about."

A power outage at the Sweeney petrochemical complex trimmed refining and chemical earnings by $21 million in the second quarter, offsetting a "blowout quarter" for Phillips' refining, marketing and transportation segment, Allen said.
The company's stock fell 6 cents to $45.31 in consolidated trading on the New York Stock Exchange Thursday afternoon.
